evidence: app/package.json:9 — hono ^4.13.14, exactly the current stable (v4.13.14 released 2026-10-25; v5 only RC, per github.com/honojs/hono/releases)
app/src/views.js:1 — html from 'hono/html', the current documented non-JSX rendering helper (hono.dev/docs/helpers/html)
app/src/server.js:1 — serve() from @hono/node-server, current API
app/src/views.js:99-103 — hx-get/hx-trigger/hx-target/hx-swap/hx-push-url, all current htmx 2.x core attributes
app/src/app.js:2 — serveStatic import path '@hono/node-server/serve-static', still correct in v2 of the adapter
app/package.json:10 — @hono/node-server ^1.19.0, superseded 1.x major; current is 2.1.5 and the 1.x line stopped before the Sept 2026 serve-static security fix
app/src/views.js:115 — interpolates the bare string 'selected' into a tag, relying on hono/html's escaping being a no-op for that literal (undocumented; docs prescribe raw())
latest_apis.rationale: Consistently on the current generation (hono 4.13.14, hono/html, htmx 2.0.11 — htmx 4.0 is not npm 'latest'), with one stale major: @hono/node-server is pinned to the 1.x line whose last release predates a published serve-static security advisory, and the 'selected' attribute trick leans on undocumented escape behavior.

evidence: app/src/api.js:16 — native global fetch for all upstream calls, no axios/node-fetch
app/src/views.js:137-146 — URLSearchParams builds filter/pagination URLs
app/src/views.js:97-103 — native form controls + htmx rather than a client framework
app/src/views.js:60 — loading="lazy" with explicit width/height on sprites
app/public/styles.css:3-70 — CSS custom properties for tokens; media query at styles.css:589
app/src/api.js:27-30 — hand-rolled regex idFromUrl instead of new URL().pathname
app/src/views.js:314-320 — sort URLs hand-concatenated as strings rather than URLSearchParams like the rest
app/src/api.js:16 — no AbortSignal.timeout on upstream fetch; a slow API hangs page renders
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first (fetch, URLSearchParams, native forms, lazy images), with small regressions: regex-based URL parsing, one hand-built query string, and no fetch timeout.

evidence: app/package.json:9-11 — exactly three runtime deps, no bundler, no CSS framework, no dev deps: lean overall
app/package.json:10 — @hono/node-server ^1.19.0 is a questionable pick: current major is 2.1.5 (2026-10-13) and v2.0.0 notes say the public API is unchanged, so the upgrade is free

app/package.json:11 vs app/src/app.js:43 — htmx.org is declared but unused at runtime: htmx.min.js is vendored in public/ and build is a no-op echo (app/package.json:6), so the dep and the served file can drift
app/src/api.js:61-75 — hand-rolled mapLimit instead of pulling a concurrency-limit package: correct restraint
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and mostly modern, but two questionable picks: an adapter pinned to the superseded 1.x major (missing a security fix shipped in 2.1.3), and an htmx dependency that nothing consumes because the file is vendored.

evidence: app/src/api.js:10-25 — all upstream I/O behind one apiFetch with runtime caching; single config point at api.js:3
app/src/api.js:79-118 — getIndex() module-level promise centralizes the derived species/type/generation index used by every page
app/src/views.js:181-184 — re-implements genus/latest-English-flavor inline although api.js:43-49 exports englishGenus/latestEnglishFlavor: spec logic in two places
app/src/views.js:186,349,379,426 and app/src/app.js:112 — identical typeEn fallback helper re-derived five times
app/package.json + app/src/api.js:10 — zero type annotations anywhere; API responses cross the boundary untyped, so shape changes surface at runtime
app/src/app.js:186-192 — the moves-table sort endpoint calls loadPokemonPageData, rebuilding species/pokemon/chain and all move fetches to re-sort one table; buildMovesData alone would do
app/src/app.js:42-44 — three hand-listed serveStatic middlewares; adding an asset means editing server code
app/src/views.js:115 — 'selected' interpolation depends on hono escaping being a no-op: breaks silently if escaping behavior changes
churn_resistance.rationale: The data-access layer is genuinely well-factored and views are pure, but there is zero typing at the API boundary, spec-critical helpers are duplicated across modules, and a couple of patterns (bare-string attributes, a full-data-rebuild sort endpoint) will need touching on the next framework or requirement move.

findings.issue: @hono/node-server pinned to ^1.19.0 (superseded 1.x major; last 1.x release 1.19.17 on 2026-07-27 predates the serveStatic path-decoding advisory GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f fixed in 2.1.3 on 2026-09-29).
findings.suggestion: Bump to ^2.1.5 — v2.0.0 release notes state the public API stays the same, so the change is a version edit.

findings.issue: htmx.org is declared as a dependency but never used: app/public/htmx.min.js is vendored and served statically (app/src/app.js:43) and `npm run build` is a no-op, so the pinned version and the served file can drift silently.
findings.suggestion: Either copy node_modules/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js in the build script, or drop the dependency and document the vendored file's version.

findings.issue: Bare-string 'selected' injected inside a tag works only because hono/html's auto-escape is a no-op for that literal — undocumented behavior; hono docs prescribe raw() for unescaped insertion.
findings.suggestion: Use ${raw('selected')} (or build the attribute conditionally) so the pattern survives escaping changes; it already leans on a near-invisible invariant.

findings.issue: Genus and latest-English-flavor logic is re-implemented inline even though api.js exports englishGenus and latestEnglishFlavor — spec-defined behavior now lives in two files.
findings.suggestion: Import the helpers from api.js and delete the inline copies.

findings.issue: No types at the API boundary (zero type annotations in the app); PokeAPI shapes flow through apiFetch untyped, so a data-shape change manifests as runtime errors scattered across views.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc @typedefs for the handful of API records (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type) and annotate apiFetch's return; pure JavaScript needs no build step to get this.

findings.issue: The table-sort endpoint rebuilds the entire Pokémon page (species, default variety, evolution chain, version-group and move fan-out) via loadPokemonPageData just to re-sort rows the client already has.
findings.suggestion: Call only buildMovesData, or sort the rendered rows client-side — sorting is pure over data already in the DOM.

findings.issue: Upstream fetch has no AbortSignal/timeout; a slow or hung API stalls every page render with no failure mode.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) to fetch and fall through to the error handler on abort.

findings.issue: Static assets are wired as three individually declared serveStatic middlewares with hardcoded paths; every new asset is a server-code edit.
findings.suggestion: One serveStatic({ root: './public' }) mounted on a static path.

findings.issue: idFromUrl parses Pokémon/species ids with a regex, and API_BASE is de-slashed with another regex, instead of the URL API the rest of the file already embraces.
findings.suggestion: Use new URL(url).pathname (and pathname-based matching) for parsing.

findings.issue: The typeEn fallback helper (index.typeEn.get(n) ?? humanize(n)) is re-derived identically in five places (views.js:186,349,379,426 and app.js:112).
findings.suggestion: Export one typeEn(index) helper and reuse it.

summary: This is a current-generation Hono + htmx app: hono 4.13.14 (the exact latest stable), the documented hono/html helper, htmx 2.0.11 (still npm 'latest'; htmx 4 is deliberately not latest), native fetch/URLSearchParams and a lean three-dependency tree. The data-access layer is well-factored and views are pure, so most future changes stay local. The deductions are a superseded 1.x pin on @hono/node-server (whose line predates a serve-static security fix), an htmx dependency that nothing consumes, an undocumented bare-string attribute trick, and zero typing at the API boundary with some duplicated spec logic.

apis.replacement: Import path is unchanged in adapter v2; only the package version is stale (see dependencies)
